I am an old woman of 76 years, and this small maize plot near my home is important for feeding my household. I have worked this land many seasons and I know maize needs food from the soil — I will buy a little DAP and urea from the cooperative like my neighbors do, though not as much as the officials recommend because money is tight. I will also spread manure from our animals, as my mother taught me. I keep seed from last year's harvest — the local maize grows well enough here and I cannot afford the new seed every year. My grandchildren and daughter-in-law help me with the weeding and harvest, and I will hire a young man with oxen for the ploughing since my back cannot manage it anymore.
